name: Typewriter Pull-Up
description: The typewriter pull-up is an advanced calisthenics variation where the lifter pulls to the top of a pull-up and then traverses horizontally across the bar — moving from side to side like a typewriter carriage — before descending. This lateral movement under full load targets the lats, biceps, and scapular stabilizers through a unique range of motion and builds exceptional pulling strength and body control.

execution.starting_position: Hang from a pull-up bar with a wide overhand grip, arms fully extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a straight pull-up bar wide enough to allow lateral movement. Ensure a solid grip on the bar.
steps: Step 1: Pull up until the chin clears the bar.
Step 2: While maintaining the top position, shift the body laterally toward the right hand by extending the left arm.
Step 3: Move fully to the right side so the chin is near the right hand.
Step 4: Traverse back across to the left side.
Step 5: Once back in the center, lower slowly to full dead hang.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale during the initial pull. Breathe steadily while traversing. Inhale on the controlled descent.
common_mistakes: Dropping from the top position before completing the traverse
Lacking the shoulder stability to control the lateral shift safely
Using a bar too narrow to allow meaningful lateral movement
safety_considerations: Ensure grip strength is sufficient — dropping from this position unexpectedly can cause injury
Only attempt after mastering controlled pull-up negatives and archer pull-ups
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from dead hang through traversal at the top.
coaching_cues: Stay at the top — do not let yourself drop during the traverse
Slide smoothly side to side rather than jerking
Engage the core hard to prevent leg swing
